title: Kula Disaster Recovery Update Meeting: January 23, 2024

recap.headline: Kula debris cleanup finished; residents press on leftover debris and insurance
recap.in_60_seconds: Maui County, federal and state officials met with Kula fire survivors for a recovery update. The Army Corps of Engineers said it finished all 25 Kula properties in the federal debris program and returned the rights of entry to the County. The SBA said its disaster loan grace period ends Thursday, and the Office of Recovery said an expedited permitting vendor should be picked by February 16 and running this spring. Five people asked questions. A Mālama Kula leader said Kula is not clean and asked who will clear debris and toxic ash outside home footprints. A resident pressed the State Insurance Commissioner on whether insurers will extend living-expense coverage to three years. Both questions, along with when gulch cleanup will start and whether permits filed now go ahead of expedited ones, were left without firm answers.

parts.title: Welcome and meeting overview
presented: The Mayor said recovery focus is shifting toward Lahaina cleanup.
The expedited permitting office has not started because the County is still contracting an outside reviewer for Kula and Lahaina applicants.
People often ask whether a permit filed now under the regular system will be handled before expedited applications; the Mayor said an answer will come.
Speakers listed: FEMA, Army Corps, SBA, County right-of-entry staff, Fire Chief, Office of Recovery and the State Insurance Commissioner.

next.what: Mayor and Office of Recovery director to announce policy on when people can apply for permits and when applications take effect

parts.title: FEMA housing and rental assistance
presented: Three property management companies are securing short-term rentals; 1,130 recipients so far, with just over 100 leased in.
Failing the required background check does not disqualify you; FEMA will find a unit under its own program.
530 have applied for continued rental assistance, 250 approved and 61 pending.
FEMA can help only after insurance additional living expense money is exhausted; call 1-800-621-3362 or visit a Disaster Recovery Center.

next.what: More FEMA housing units becoming available
next.when: within the next couple of months

parts.title: Army Corps debris removal completion
parts.presenter: Army Corps of Engineers Maui recovery commander
presented: All 25 Kula properties in the federal program are done; final tree removal and mulching finished in early January.
Rights of entry were returned to the County, so the Corps no longer has legal access to those properties; property reports are being finalized.
The Corps thanked residents and the Council Member and said the hardest job needed a large crane on a hillside.
Lahaina work started last week; six properties were cleared and tested as of yesterday.

parts.title: Closeout packages and soil reports
presented: Owners can request their closeout package: a certificate that the property was deemed clean plus photographs.
An online map to download packages is in development.
Soil test reports, including results after any rescrape, come from the Army Corps call center at 877-214-9117.
Staff said Kula helped build in two to three weeks a process that might have taken the County two to three years.

next.what: Online map to download closeout packages
next.when: by the time Lahaina properties are done

parts.title: SBA disaster loans
presented: The grace period for physical disaster loans for homeowners, renters, businesses and nonprofits ends Thursday; later applications need an explanation.
SBA has approved a little over $290 million in loans.
Help is available at the Lahaina Civic Center, the Kīhei recovery center, the Kahului Public Library and online.

next.what: SBA physical disaster loan grace period ends

parts.title: Underground hot spots and fire preparedness
presented: Underground fires in roots and organic material are still burning; well over a dozen broke the surface and ignited.
Call 911 if you smell smoke; trucks carry thermal imagers that work best in cool morning or evening hours.
Do not pile green waste or tree trimmings on burned ground; a recent Kula fire started that way.
The Fire Prevention Bureau has three to five times its normal requests, so responses take two to three weeks; Ready, Set, Go booklets and the Wildland Urban Interface program are available.

parts.title: Office of Recovery and expedited permitting
parts.presenter: Deputy Director of the Office of Recovery and County meeting moderator
presented: The Office of Recovery is developing a long-term recovery plan; a joint county, state and federal needs assessment is done and documents are on mauirecovers.org.
The expedited permitting proposal request closed January 8; vendor interviews are underway.
Vendor selection is set for February 16, with the office hoped to be operating this spring; Kula applicants will go through first.
The County will return next week to gather Kula needs, with the Council Member and the Kula Community Watershed Alliance; a QR code survey was posted.

next.what: Kula meeting to gather community needs

parts.title: State Insurance Division update
presented: An emergency declaration on August 9 let emergency adjusters work; Insurance Division staff were at the recovery center daily until January 5.
As of November 30, about $1.7 billion in property claims were filed and nearly $1.2 billion, about 73%, paid.
About $30 million in vehicle claims, with over $29 million, or 97%, paid and closed.
A December 31 data update is coming; a guide on insurance and debris removal is available.

next.what: Updated insurance claims data as of December 31

raised.concern: Insurers have not said whether they will honor the Commissioner's September letter asking them to extend additional living expenses to three years, so fire survivors cannot set rebuilding budgets.
Why Hawaiʻi cannot require insurers to extend living expenses as California did after its wildfires.

Kula is not clean: scrap metal, toxic ash and debris outside home footprints remain, runoff carries colored soil into streets and gulches, and tests found heavy metals in standing homes; who cleans up, what are the liability risks for volunteers, and will there be a community-advised phase three.
The QR code survey said it was not accepting responses.
When will toxic debris in the gulch be cleaned up, and does someone have a paid contract for it.
Conflicting information on whether the first $25,000 of an approved SBA loan requires receipts before it is paid out.
Whether the expedited permitting vendors will also help the water department.

answered.said: Some larger insurers said they intend to comply, but coverage depends on each policy; some limit living expenses to one year with no dollar cap. People can call the Insurance Division to review their policy.

Hawaiʻi law gives him no authority to mandate payments, and courts, not his office, interpret policies. Bills on living expenses and personal property payments are before the Legislature, which started last week.
He asked insurers to extend coverage because recovery will be long, and is working with the state emergency agency and FEMA to get insurers to send exhaustion forms so people can get FEMA housing.
Federal partners finished the work they were assigned and funded to do; the remaining gaps are why the County returns next week.
There is no answer on the gulch tonight; it will be part of next week's discussion.
The gulch falls under a federal NRCS emergency watershed program with $2.7 million allocated, but work has not started and may not cover every gulch.
Loans are case by case; SBA will look into the individual application after the meeting. Approved borrowers can also ask to delay disbursement.

answered.who: Deputy Director of the Office of Recovery
answered.said: Yes, the vendors will help the water department with permits.
Answering a Council Member, he said people without insurance are served by other state, county and federal programs, not his office.

She believes NRCS awarded about $15 million to the Soil and Water Conservation District for burned areas, including the gulch, but was unsure of the figure. She urged residents to harden homes and said FEMA has hazard mitigation grants.
The QR code is working now.

next.what: FEMA administrators visit Maui; Council Member to raise hazard mitigation grants

parts.title: Mayor's closing remarks
presented: The Mayor said the Corps, EPA and search and rescue all finished ahead of schedule, using local contractors.
He said the County is not done and is moving from emergency work to recovery.
Next steps are federal HUD disaster funds and requests to the Legislature.

answered.said: He will go to the Governor about work in Kula that is not finished, while also helping Lahaina, and will seek state, county or philanthropic help if needed.

next.what: Mayor to raise unfinished Kula work with the Governor
County to seek recovery funds from the Legislature and HUD

bills.name: Long-term recovery plan
bills.what: A plan the County Office of Recovery is developing with the community to guide long-term recovery from the August fires.

bills.name: Article 13 of the state insurance code
bills.what: The state law on unfair and deceptive practices and claim payment that the Insurance Division uses to check insurer compliance.

open_questions.question: Will permits filed now under the regular system be processed before applications to the new expedited office?
After the Army Corps finished, who will clean up debris, scrap metal and toxic ash outside home footprints in Kula, and will there be a phase three?
When will cleanup of toxic debris in the Kula gulches begin, and who is contracted to do it?
Will insurers honor the Insurance Commissioner's request to extend additional living expenses to three years?
Does the first $25,000 of an approved SBA disaster loan require receipts before disbursement?

not_on_tracker.topic: Leftover debris and toxic ash outside home footprints in Kula
not_on_tracker.why: Volunteers are clearing it at their own cost and risk, and runoff is carrying contaminated soil into streets and gulches.
Fire survivors whose coverage ends after one year cannot plan how much to spend on rebuilding versus rent.
Residents want to know when funded federal cleanup will start.

not_on_tracker.topic: Expedited rebuilding permit office timing and order
not_on_tracker.why: Kula owners ready to rebuild need to know whether to file now or wait.

not_on_tracker.topic: Underground hot spots in the Kula burn area
not_on_tracker.why: Hidden fires are still surfacing and igniting yard waste piles.
Borrowers got conflicting information on receipts before construction can start.
